# fjordrun_tcp_proxy (Resource)

A public TCP port for a `web`, `worker` or `database` service: clients connect to `host:port`, forwarded to `target_port`. Hobby plan or higher, up to 5 per service, and not with `sleep_when_idle` (TCP connections don't wake a sleeping service). The API can't change one: `target_port` replaces it, and the replacement gets a new public port.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "fjordrun_project" "shop" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "shop"
}

resource "fjordrun_service" "db" {
  project_id     = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_project.shop.default_environment_id
  name           = "db"
  kind           = "database"
  source         = { type = "image", image = "postgres:17" }
  deploy         = { port = 5432 }
}

resource "fjordrun_tcp_proxy" "db" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_service.db.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_service.db.environment_id
  target_port    = 5432
}

output "database_address" {
  value = "${fjordrun_tcp_proxy.db.host}:${fjordrun_tcp_proxy.db.port}"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID.
- `service_id` (String) Service ID.
- `target_port` (Number) The port the service listens on (1-65535).

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time.
- `host` (String) Host clients connect to.
- `id` (String) Public TCP port ID.
- `port` (Number) Port clients connect to, assigned from 20000-29999.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# service_id/environment_id/proxy_id
terraform import fjordrun_tcp_proxy.db 77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777/66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666/aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa
```
